title: hardening: VS Code's verified-local pin is session-only, so a project.json edit between sessions downgrades a protected project to legacy with no confirmation (no RF02 parity)
description:
Found by CQ-RF07 (task-f3f364a6), the epic-final adversarial review; RF06 (task-98ffe33f) listed it as a known gap.

Evidence at 28df02f7: moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts runtimeProfile() pins a verified-local read only in the in-memory pinnedProjects set. Nothing persists. After a VS Code restart, a project.json that now says legacy (or omits executionProfile), for example after a git pull or checkout, gives 'legacy' with no prompt. JetBrains (RF02) persists the confirmed profile in its owner-only store and asks "Moe: Execution Profile Downgrade" (Keep Protected / Allow Downgrade) before any downgrade, effective only after a restart.

Scenario: a protected project is opened in VS Code, and the repository then flips the declaration between sessions. The next session launches agents through resolveAgentScript (repository/PATH copies) and the legacy daemon start, which are the runtimes the protected profile exists to exclude.
definitionOfDone: VS Code persists a confirmed protected profile outside the repository, owner-only (a store under the extension's globalStorage or the OS user state, never the workspace), and a weaker or untrusted declaration of a project recorded as protected stays protected until an explicit, safe-default human confirmation; an allowed downgrade takes effect only after a restart.
An unreadable, foreign or untrusted record reads as protected; a store that cannot be proved outside the project persists nothing new.

LEGACY projects never prompt; the existing moe-vscode tests are unchanged and new tests cover persist, ask, decline, dismiss and untrusted-record cases; `cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile` exits 0 on Linux and on Windows.
taskRails: Protected-profile state lives outside the repository, owner-only; a missing, unreadable or mismatched record fails closed to protected.

implementationPlan.description:
RED tests first (test-driven-development). Create moe-vscode/tests/protected-profile-pin.test.cjs with the Write tool. Build the harness on tests/protected-runtime.test.cjs and protected-daemon-spawn.test.cjs: transpile src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts and run it in vm.runInNewContext with a permissive require map. Pass Buffer and process. vscode.window.showWarningMessage records (message, options, ...items) and resolves f.choice (default undefined).

A RESTART is a fresh vm load of the module against the same store directory, so the module-level session pin resets. Each fixture uses a temp project, plus a store root OUTSIDE it set through f.api.useProtectedStateRoot(root). Cases:
(P1) Persist. Session 1 reads a verified-local project.json and gets 'protected'. It writes exactly one record file under root, named by protectedStateName('profile', key) as 16 hex characters plus '.json', so no input reaches the name. The record is {"version":1,"project":<key>,"profile":"protected"}. On POSIX the file mode is 0600 and the root's is 0700.
(P2) Ask. Session 2, after project.json flipped to legacy or lost executionProfile, gets 'protected' and asks once: a modal showWarningMessage with exactly 'Keep Protected' and 'Allow Downgrade', and text naming the folder and the after-restart rule. More runtimeProfile calls in that session ask nothing more.
(P3) Decline with 'Keep Protected': the record stays protected, and session 3 asks again and stays protected.
(P4) Dismiss (undefined): the same as decline.
(P5) Allow with 'Allow Downgrade': session 2 still answers 'protected' (it takes effect only after a restart). The record becomes 'legacy'. Session 3 answers 'legacy' with no prompt.
(P6) Untrusted record. With a legacy declaration, each of these answers 'protected' and asks: malformed JSON; an extra field; version 2; another project's key; profile 'observe'; a record file larger than 64 KiB; and on POSIX, a 0644 file, a 0755 root, and a symlinked record or root.
(P7) A store root INSIDE the project: a verified-local read writes nothing (no file is created anywhere under the root), and still answers 'protected' for the session.
(P8) A LEGACY project with no record never prompts and writes nothing.
(P9) With no store root configured, behavior is exactly today's: session pin only, no prompt, no writes.
(P10) An unreadable or invalid project.json still answers 'protected' with no prompt, as today.

RED: run `node --test tests/protected-profile-pin.test.cjs` in the step-4 Linux snapshot with only this file overlaid. The new cases must fail against the unchanged client. Quote the failures in complete_step.
implementationPlan.note: RED: created moe-vscode/tests/protected-profile-pin.test.cjs (Write tool). 30 cases: P1 persist (FNV-1a 64 name checked against a test-side reference validated on the published vectors '' and 'a'; record bytes; 0600/0700), P2 x3 flips (legacy / no executionProfile / no project.json) ask once, modal, exact buttons and text; P3/P4 x5 (Keep, dismiss, another label, rejected prompt, throwing prompt) keep the record untouched (same inode) and re-ask next session; P5 allow records legacy, the session stays protected, restart answers legacy, verified-local re-protects; P6 x15 untrusted records (malformed, extra/missing field, v2, foreign key, observe, array, BOM, >64 KiB, record is a dir, root is a file; POSIX 0644 file, 0755 root, symlinked record, symlinked root) answer protected + ask, and no SECRET content reaches a log; P7 root inside the project writes nothing; P8 legacy no record never prompts or creates the root; P9 no root = session-only; P10 untrusted declaration protected, no prompt, no pin, no write; S1 store round-trip, name refusal, oversize refusal, no temp file left after a failed rename. RED run in Linux snapshot /tmp/moe-98c8-red-bn8L (git archive HEAD b99e31c2 + this file overlaid, cmp ok, npm ci exit 0): `node --test tests/protected-profile-pin.test.cjs` -> all 30 fail, each with `TypeError: api.useProtectedStateRoot is not a function` (the store API does not exist yet).

implementationPlan.description:
The owner-only store (DoD 1-2; the epic and task rails on owner-only state). It mirrors JetBrains util/ProtectedStateStore.kt, and task-648a5916 reuses it for daemon spawn records, so keep this API exactly. Module-level in moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts, next to runtimeProfile:

- `export function useProtectedStateRoot(dir: string | undefined): void` sets the root. moe-vscode/src/extension.ts calls `useProtectedStateRoot(path.join(context.globalStorageUri.fsPath, 'protected-state'))` as the FIRST statement of activate(), before the client is constructed or anything reads runtimeProfile. globalStorage is per user and outside every workspace.
- `export function projectStateKey(basePath: string): string` is the expression runtimeProfile uses today: comparablePath(realPathOrNull(base) ?? path.resolve(base), defaultFoldCase). Extract it and reuse it there.
- `export function protectedStateName(kind: string, projectKey: string): string` is FNV-1a 64 (BigInt) over the UTF-8 bytes of `${kind}:${projectKey}`, as 16 lowercase hex characters plus '.json'. It is non-cryptographic on purpose: node:crypto cannot be loaded synchronously here without a top-level import, and three suites load this file through a closed require map (accounts-wire, plan-approval-client, task-notifier: vscode, ws, child_process, fs, path, net only). So add NO new top-level import. Every record carries its project key and is checked on read, so a collision reads as foreign, which means protected (fail closed).
- `export function readProtectedState(name: string): string | undefined` returns undefined when no root is set, the root is absent, or the file is absent. It THROWS an Error for state this extension would not have written:
  - the root or file is not a plain directory or regular file under lstat (a link is refused);
  - on POSIX: the root's mode & 0o777 !== 0o700, the file's !== 0o600, or a uid other than process.getuid();
  - the file is larger than 64 KiB.
  The error message names the broken rule, never the contents.
- `export function writeProtectedState(name: string, text: string, basePath: string): boolean` writes only when isOutsideProject(root, basePath) holds; otherwise it logs and returns false. It does mkdirSync(root, { recursive: true, mode: 0o700 }), then chmod 0o700 and re-verifies on POSIX. It writes a temp file in the root opened 'wx' with mode 0o600, then renameSync over the target. On failure it deletes the temp file and returns false. It never throws.
- On Windows, Node has no ACL API, so the per-user profile location (globalStorage) is the owner-only boundary. State that in a comment; the link, kind and size checks still apply.

Error handling: every fs call is inside try/catch. read reports untrusted state by throwing (the caller fails closed); write reports failure by returning false.
implementationPlan.note: Store API added to MoeDaemonClient.ts next to runtimeProfile, with exactly the planned names and signatures: useProtectedStateRoot(dir|undefined), projectStateKey(base) (extracted; runtimeProfile now calls it), protectedStateName(kind, key) = FNV-1a 64 BigInt over UTF-8 `${kind}:${key}` -> 16 hex + '.json', readProtectedState(name) (undefined for no root / absent root / absent file; throws for a name that is not 16 hex + .json, a non-plain-directory root or non-regular file under lstat (links refused), POSIX mode != 0700/0600 or a foreign uid, >64 KiB; opens with O_NOFOLLOW where available and re-checks fstat), writeProtectedState(name, text, base) (false + log unless isOutsideProject(root, base); size cap; mkdir 0700 + chmod on a plain dir + re-verify; temp opened 'wx' 0600 + fchmod, renameSync; temp removed on failure; never throws). readCappedText's body moved into readCappedFd(fd, ...) so the store reuses the capped read (no behavior change). Windows comment: no ACL API in Node, globalStorage is the owner-only boundary. No new top-level import. extension.ts: imports useProtectedStateRoot from the existing MoeDaemonClient import and calls useProtectedStateRoot(path.join(context.globalStorageUri.fsPath, 'protected-state')) as the first statement of activate(). Deliberately skipped: JetBrains requireDirectoryAbove (a root BELOW a regular file on Windows reads absent) - deleting the record has the same effect, so it adds no protection. Snapshot /tmp/moe-98c8-red-bn8L with the 3 files overlaid (cmp ok): new suite 30 tests, 4 pass (S1 store round-trip/name/size/temp cleanup now green), 26 fail pending step 3; `tsc -p ./ --noEmit` exit 0.

implementationPlan.description:
The RF02 pin in runtimeProfile (DoD 1-3). It mirrors JetBrains RuntimeSelectionPolicy.profile, storedProfile, persist and askDowngrade, and ProfileDowngradeDialog. runtimeProfile stays synchronous and never throws:
1. A blank base is 'legacy'. A key in pinnedProjects is 'protected'.
2. A declaration read that throws is 'protected', as today: log, no pin, no write.
3. stored = ABSENT | LEGACY | PROTECTED | UNTRUSTED. ABSENT means no root or no file. A strict parse of the record requires exactly {version, project, profile}, version 1, project === key and profile 'protected' or 'legacy'. Any read throw or parse failure is UNTRUSTED, logged.
4. A verified-local declaration pins the key and, unless stored is PROTECTED, writes {"version":1,"project":key,"profile":"protected"} via writeProtectedState(protectedStateName('profile', key), text, base).
5. Otherwise, ABSENT or LEGACY answers 'legacy', unless the key was pinned meanwhile.
6. Otherwise (PROTECTED or UNTRUSTED), pin the key. The first time in a session, call the confirmer without awaiting it: `void vscode.window.showWarningMessage(message, { modal: true }, 'Keep Protected', 'Allow Downgrade')`, with `.then(choice => ...)` and a catch.
   - The message is: '<folder name> now declares the legacy execution profile, but it was confirmed protected. Moe keeps it protected until you allow the downgrade. An allowed downgrade takes effect after you restart VS Code.'
   - Only exactly 'Allow Downgrade' writes profile 'legacy'. 'Keep Protected', dismissal, a rejection or an exception keep protected, and are logged.
   - The session pin keeps this session protected either way, so an allowed downgrade takes effect only after a restart.
   Return 'protected'.

LEGACY projects never reach step 6, so they never prompt. With no root (the existing tests), steps 3-6 reduce to today's session behavior.

Error handling: the confirmer's promise always has a catch, and a failing write only logs. Nothing here makes a LEGACY project protected except an existing record that is PROTECTED or UNTRUSTED.
implementationPlan.note: RF02 pin in runtimeProfile, synchronous, never throws: blank -> legacy; session pin -> protected; a declaration read that throws -> protected via the existing catch (no pin, no store read, no write); storedProfile(key) = absent (no root, short-circuited before hashing so closed-map suites never touch Buffer, or no file) | legacy | protected | untrusted (any read throw; JSON.parse failure logged as a fixed rule string so record contents never reach the log; keys not exactly version/project/profile; version !== 1; project !== key; profile not protected/legacy). verified-local pins and persists {"version":1,"project":key,"profile":"protected"} unless already PROTECTED. Otherwise ABSENT/LEGACY -> legacy; PROTECTED/UNTRUSTED pins and calls askDowngrade once (the pin makes later calls return early): `void Promise.resolve(vscode.window.showWarningMessage(message, { modal: true }, 'Keep Protected', 'Allow Downgrade')).then(...).catch(...)` inside try/catch; only exactly 'Allow Downgrade' writes legacy; keep/dismiss/other/reject/throw log 'Moe keeps the protected profile'. Message text exactly as planned. Skipped the "pinned meanwhile" re-check from plan item 5: runtimeProfile is synchronous JS, nothing can pin between the top check and the store read. GREEN in snapshot /tmp/moe-98c8-red-bn8L (3 files overlaid, cmp ok): protected-profile-pin 30/30 pass; full `npm test` 622 tests, 618 pass, 0 fail, 4 skipped; `tsc -p ./ --noEmit` exit 0; `npm run lint` exit 0.

Windows leg (cmd.exe, node v24.16.0, D:\moe-scratch\98c81a27-win-1793661073\moe-vscode): `npm ci --no-audit --no-fund && npm test && npm run compile` exit 0 -> tests 618, pass 613, fail 0, skipped 5 (all 5 pre-existing symlink/NTFS skips); new suite 26/26 (the 4 POSIX-only P6 cases are not registered on Windows: 0644 record, 0755 root, symlinked record, symlinked root). Base without this row = 592 tests on Linux (622 - 30).

Adversarial self-review of `git diff -- moe-vscode/src/services/MoeDaemonClient.ts moe-vscode/src/extension.ts` + the new test (no code change resulted).
(a) Fail closed: a non-verified-local declaration answers 'legacy' only from stored 'absent'/'legacy'; every read throw or parse failure is 'untrusted' -> protected + ask. A thrown or rejected prompt, a dismissal, Keep and any other label never write (P3/P4 x5: same inode after settle). An unreadable declaration still returns protected through the existing catch before any store access.
(b) Restart: the key is pinned before askDowngrade and is never removed, so an allow only writes 'legacy' for the next load (P5).
(c) Store: names must match /^[0-9a-f]{16}\.json$/ (both read and write), produced only by protectedStateName. lstat refuses links, kinds, POSIX mode != 0700/0600 and foreign uid. The read opens with O_NOFOLLOW where available and re-checks fstat, capped at 64 KiB. The write uses a 'wx' 0600 temp in the root plus renameSync, and the temp is removed on any failure (S1: a rename onto a directory leaves only the two expected entries). A root inside the project writes nothing (P7).
(d) Two windows: separate temp names (pid + serial) and atomic rename, so the last writer wins with a whole record. A torn or empty file after a crash reads untrusted, which means protected.
(e) The import block is unchanged (vscode, fs, path, net, type http, child_process, ws). accounts-wire, plan-approval-client and task-notifier pass in both legs. storedProfile and persistProfile return before protectedStateName when no root is set, so contexts without Buffer never hash.
(f) Mutations in scratch /tmp/moe-98c8-mut-Injo (the Linux snapshot's src+tests, node_modules linked), each run with `node --test tests/protected-profile-pin.test.cjs`:
- M1, untrusted read as legacy: 15 fail, all P6;
- M2, Keep treated as allow: 1 fail, P3/P4 (Keep Protected);
- M3, inside-project guard dropped: 1 fail, P7;
- M4, pin deleted on allow: 1 fail, P5.
The restored copy (cmp equal to the worktree) passes 30/30.
Theoretical only, accepted with parity to JetBrains:
- On Windows, a link swapped in between lstat and open is not refused (no O_NOFOLLOW), and a swap of the root's parent is unchecked on any OS. Both need write access to the user's own globalStorage, and with that access the record could simply be deleted (absent).
- A root left at the wrong mode or owner (for example a no-metadata mount, or created under sudo) makes every legacy project read untrusted and prompt. JetBrains checks the root first in the same way. The log names the rule.
- No fsync: a power loss reads untrusted, which fails closed.
(g) task-648a5916 reuses: useProtectedStateRoot(dir), projectStateKey(base), protectedStateName(kind, key) (16 hex + .json), readProtectedState(name) (undefined, or throws for untrusted) and writeProtectedState(name, text, base) (boolean, never throws). Use kind 'spawn'.

executionContract.intendedBehavior: A project VS Code once read as verified-local stays protected across restarts. Its confirmed profile is persisted in an owner-only record outside the repository (globalStorage/protected-state). A later weaker or untrusted declaration asks 'Keep Protected' / 'Allow Downgrade'; only an explicit allow records legacy, and it takes effect after a restart. Untrusted records read as protected, a store that is not provably outside the project persists nothing, and LEGACY projects never prompt.
acceptanceCriteria: tests/protected-profile-pin.test.cjs covers persist, ask, decline, dismiss, allow-after-restart, untrusted record, store inside the project, legacy no-prompt, no store root (today's behavior) and an untrusted declaration, RED first.
`cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile` exits 0 on Linux and on Windows.
invariants: Only an explicit 'Allow Downgrade' ever records legacy; nothing downgrades within the session.
No new top-level import in MoeDaemonClient.ts.
With no store root configured, behavior equals today's.
compatibility: The store API is reused by task-648a5916 for spawn records (kind 'spawn').
Every existing moe-vscode test passes unchanged.
approvedScope: The module-level store API in MoeDaemonClient.ts (useProtectedStateRoot, projectStateKey, protectedStateName, readProtectedState, writeProtectedState) plus the RF02 logic inside runtimeProfile and its downgrade confirmer.
checkRefs: cd moe-vscode && npm test && npm run compile (Linux snapshot and Windows snapshot, per step 4)

planningNotes.approachesConsidered: 1) SecretStorage. Rejected for the pin: it is async, while runtimeProfile is synchronous and called from connect, AgentLauncher and ManagedVmTreeProvider. A preload race would read 'legacy' first, or need awaits added at every caller. 2) A single profiles.json map. Rejected: a read-modify-write across two windows can drop another project's pin (fail-open). 3) Per-record files in an owner-only root under globalStorage, CHOSEN. This mirrors JetBrains ProtectedStateStore, and the DoD names globalStorage. task-648a5916 will be re-planned to reuse this store for its spawn records, so there is one store, as in JetBrains (RF02 reused RF01's store). 4) sha256 names. Rejected: no synchronous crypto without a top-level import, and three suites load the file through a closed require map. FNV-1a 64 plus an in-record project check fails closed on a collision.
planningNotes.codebaseInsights: runtimeProfile (MoeDaemonClient.ts ~:297) pins only in the module-level pinnedProjects set. isOutsideProject (~:438) already handles realpath, alias and missing paths. The vm harnesses re-load the module per fixture, so a fresh load simulates a restart. extension.ts activate() is synchronous and constructs the client at :35. The JetBrains references are RuntimeSelectionPolicy.profile/storedProfile/askDowngrade, ProfileDowngradeDialog (text and buttons) and ProtectedStateStore (owner-only rules, 64 KiB cap, atomic write).
planningNotes.risks: (1) A top-level import breaks the accounts-wire, plan-approval-client and task-notifier suites. (2) POSIX mode assertions must skip on Windows, and Node has no ACL API there; document it. (3) The modal is fire-and-forget, so tests must await the confirmer's settlement (a flush of microtasks or setImmediate) before asserting writes. (4) task-648a5916 will depend on this row and reuse its store API, so keep the names and signatures exactly as planned.

completionSummary:
VS Code RF02 parity: a confirmed verified-local project stays protected across restarts.

Store (MoeDaemonClient.ts, module level, no new top-level import). This API is reused by task-648a5916 with kind 'spawn':
- useProtectedStateRoot
- projectStateKey
- protectedStateName: FNV-1a 64 of kind:key, 16 hex + .json
- readProtectedState: undefined when absent. It throws for a link, the wrong kind, POSIX mode != 0700/0600, a foreign uid, more than 64 KiB, or a bad name.
- writeProtectedState: writes only in a root provably outside the project, as a 'wx' 0600 temp plus rename, and never throws.

- ABSENT or LEGACY records answer legacy with no prompt;
- with no root, behavior is unchanged.
